topicName: Development of Technology (Stone Age to Iron Age)
description: This topic traces how early humans developed tools and technology from the Stone Age through to the Iron Age, including the use of fire and iron smelting, and how these changes transformed human life.

mcq.questionText: What main material was used to make tools during the Stone Age?
mcq.explanation: The Stone Age is named after stone, the main hard material early humans used to make their tools and weapons.

mcq.questionText: The Old Stone Age period is also known by which scientific name?
mcq.explanation: Palaeolithic means 'old stone' and refers to the earliest and longest stage of the Stone Age.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the main way of getting food during the Old Stone Age?

options.text: Hunting wild animals and gathering wild fruits

mcq.explanation: During the Old Stone Age, people survived mainly by hunting wild animals and gathering wild plants, fruits and roots.

mcq.questionText: The New Stone Age (Neolithic) is most associated with which major change in human life?

options.text: The beginning of farming and settled life
The building of large cities with cars

mcq.explanation: In the Neolithic period people began to grow crops and keep animals, which allowed them to settle in one place instead of wandering.

mcq.questionText: Which period of the Stone Age came between the Old Stone Age and the New Stone Age?
mcq.explanation: The Mesolithic, or Middle Stone Age, was the transitional period between the Old and New Stone Ages.

mcq.questionText: Which of these tools is typical of the New Stone Age compared with the Old Stone Age?

options.text: Smooth, well-polished and sharpened stone tools

mcq.explanation: New Stone Age people improved their skills and produced smooth, polished and sharper stone tools than the rough tools of the Old Stone Age.

mcq.questionText: The discovery of fire by early humans helped them mainly to do what?

options.text: Cook food, give warmth and scare away wild animals
Make iron tools directly from stone
Send messages over long distances by phone

mcq.explanation: Fire allowed early people to cook food, keep warm, provide light and protect themselves from dangerous wild animals.

mcq.questionText: Which age came immediately after the Stone Age in many parts of Africa?
mcq.explanation: In much of Africa the Stone Age was followed by the Iron Age, when people learned to make tools from iron.

mcq.questionText: The process of heating iron ore to remove the metal from the rock is called?
mcq.explanation: Iron smelting is the process of heating iron ore in a furnace at high temperatures to separate the iron metal from the rock.

mcq.questionText: Why were iron tools more useful than stone tools for farming?

options.text: They were heavier and harder to carry
They were sharper, stronger and could be shaped into different tools
They could not break at all and never needed sharpening
They were made without any heat

mcq.explanation: Iron tools were sharper, more durable and could be shaped into hoes, axes and knives, making farming and other work easier.

mcq.questionText: Which group of people benefited most directly from the invention of the iron hoe?
mcq.explanation: The iron hoe made it much easier to dig and prepare land, greatly helping farmers to increase their food production.

mcq.questionText: How did the development of farming during the New Stone Age affect human settlement?

options.text: People moved around even more than before
People began to settle permanently in villages
People returned to living only in caves

mcq.explanation: Because crops needed care and harvesting in one place, farming encouraged people to settle permanently and form villages.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an effect of technological development from the Stone Age to the Iron Age?

options.text: Food production increased and life became easier
Humans lost the ability to use fire

mcq.explanation: Better tools and methods raised food production, improved security and made daily human life easier and more settled.

mcq.questionText: Domestication of animals during the Stone Age means that people began to?

options.text: Hunt all wild animals to extinction
Tame and keep animals such as goats and cattle for their use

mcq.explanation: Domestication means taming wild animals and keeping them for meat, milk, skins and labour instead of only hunting them.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly shows the order of technological ages from earliest to latest?

options.text: Iron Age, Old Stone Age, New Stone Age
Old Stone Age, Middle Stone Age, New Stone Age, Iron Age
New Stone Age, Iron Age, Old Stone Age
Iron Age, New Stone Age, Middle Stone Age, Old Stone Age

mcq.explanation: Technology developed in the order Old Stone Age, Middle Stone Age, New Stone Age and finally the Iron Age.

fib.questionText: The earliest and longest stage of the Stone Age is scientifically called the _____ period.
fib.explanation: Palaeolithic means 'old stone' and refers to the Old Stone Age, the first stage of human technology.

fib.questionText: The New Stone Age is also known by the scientific name _____.
fib.explanation: Neolithic means 'new stone' and is the period when farming and polished tools developed.

fib.questionText: During the Old Stone Age, people obtained their food mainly through hunting and _____.
fib.explanation: Early people gathered wild fruits, roots and plants in addition to hunting animals for food.

fib.questionText: The process of heating iron ore in a furnace to get metal is called iron _____.
fib.explanation: Iron smelting separates the iron metal from the rock by heating the ore to very high temperatures.

fib.questionText: The discovery of _____ allowed early humans to cook food and keep warm.
fib.explanation: Fire was used for cooking, warmth, light and protection against wild animals.

fib.questionText: The age that followed the Stone Age in Africa, when people made tools from metal, is the _____ Age.
fib.explanation: The Iron Age came after the Stone Age, when humans learned to make tools and weapons from iron.

fib.questionText: The taming and keeping of wild animals such as goats and cattle is called _____ of animals.
fib.explanation: Domestication allowed people to keep animals for meat, milk and labour instead of only hunting them.

fib.questionText: The Middle Stone Age is scientifically known as the _____ period.
fib.explanation: The Mesolithic was the transitional period between the Old and New Stone Ages.

fib.questionText: Compared to Old Stone Age tools, New Stone Age tools were smooth and _____.
fib.explanation: New Stone Age people improved their skills to produce smoother, polished and sharper stone tools.

fib.questionText: The main iron farming tool that made digging and cultivation easier was the iron _____.
fib.explanation: The iron hoe greatly improved farming by making it easier to dig and prepare the land.

tf.questionText: The Stone Age got its name because tools during that time were mainly made from stone.
tf.explanation: Stone was the main hard material used to make tools and weapons during the Stone Age.

tf.questionText: The Iron Age came before the Old Stone Age in the development of technology.
tf.explanation: The Old Stone Age was the earliest period, and the Iron Age came much later after the Stone Age.

tf.questionText: During the Old Stone Age people were mainly farmers who grew crops in permanent villages.
tf.explanation: Old Stone Age people were hunters and gatherers who moved around; farming and settled villages came later.

tf.questionText: The discovery of fire helped early humans to protect themselves from wild animals.
tf.explanation: Wild animals feared fire, so early humans used it for protection as well as for warmth and cooking.

tf.questionText: Iron smelting involves heating iron ore to remove the iron metal from the rock.
tf.explanation: Smelting heats the ore to very high temperatures so that the iron metal can be separated from the rock.

tf.questionText: New Stone Age tools were rougher and less sharp than Old Stone Age tools.
tf.explanation: New Stone Age tools were actually smoother, more polished and sharper than the rough Old Stone Age tools.

tf.questionText: The development of farming encouraged people to settle permanently in one place.
tf.explanation: Because crops needed care and harvesting in one place, farming led to permanent settlements and villages.

tf.questionText: Iron tools were generally weaker and broke more easily than stone tools.
tf.explanation: Iron tools were stronger, sharper and more durable than stone tools, making work easier.

tf.questionText: The Mesolithic period is the same as the Middle Stone Age.
tf.explanation: Mesolithic means 'middle stone' and refers to the Middle Stone Age between the Old and New Stone Ages.

tf.questionText: Technological development from the Stone Age to the Iron Age generally made human life harder and reduced food production.
tf.explanation: Better tools and methods increased food production and made human life easier, not harder.

summary.questionText: Main material of the Stone Age
summary.explanation: Tools and weapons were mainly made from stone, giving the age its name.

summary.questionText: Three stages of the Stone Age
summary.correctAnswer: Old (Palaeolithic), Middle (Mesolithic) and New (Neolithic) Stone Age
summary.explanation: The Stone Age is divided into these three main stages based on tool development.

summary.questionText: Way of life in the Old Stone Age
summary.explanation: People survived by hunting wild animals and gathering wild plants and fruits.

summary.questionText: Major change in the New Stone Age
summary.correctAnswer: Beginning of farming and settled life
summary.explanation: People started growing crops and keeping animals, leading to permanent settlements.

summary.questionText: Uses of fire by early humans
summary.correctAnswer: Cooking, warmth, light and protection from wild animals
summary.explanation: Fire was one of the most important early discoveries that improved human life.

summary.correctAnswer: Heating iron ore to get iron metal from the rock
summary.explanation: Smelting separated the iron metal so it could be shaped into tools.

summary.questionText: Advantages of iron tools over stone tools
summary.correctAnswer: Sharper, stronger, more durable and easy to shape
summary.explanation: These qualities made iron tools better for farming, hunting and other work.

summary.correctAnswer: Taming and keeping wild animals for human use
summary.explanation: Animals were kept for meat, milk, skins and labour instead of only hunting them.

summary.questionText: The age that followed the Stone Age
summary.explanation: In the Iron Age people learned to make tools and weapons from iron.

summary.questionText: Main effects of technological development on human life
summary.correctAnswer: Increased food production, settled life and easier work
summary.explanation: Better tools and methods improved food supply, security and daily living.

hoq.questionText: Why is the move from hunting and gathering to farming considered one of the most important changes in human history?

options.text: It forced people to stop using any tools
It produced a steady food supply that allowed permanent settlement and population growth
It made people travel more and settle less
It immediately ended the use of fire

hoq.explanation: Farming gave a reliable food supply, which allowed people to settle permanently, grow in number and develop more complex societies.

hoq.questionText: How did the discovery of iron smelting lead to greater changes in society than improvements in stone tools alone?

options.text: Iron could be shaped into many strong, sharp tools that boosted farming, warfare and trade
Iron tools were only used for decoration and nothing else
Iron smelting made people abandon farming forever
Iron tools could not be sharpened or reshaped

hoq.explanation: Because iron is strong and can be reshaped, it produced better hoes, axes and weapons that increased food production, strengthened armies and encouraged trade.

hoq.questionText: A community changes from rough stone tools to polished tools, then to iron tools, while its population and villages grow steadily. What does this pattern best illustrate?

options.text: That technology had no effect on how people lived
That improving technology and growing, more settled societies developed together
That people were becoming less skilled over time
That farming caused tools to disappear

hoq.explanation: The pattern shows that as tool technology improved, food production and security increased, allowing populations and settlements to grow alongside it.
